players.product: AWG/PLC passive optical chips and WDM components, MT-FA/FAU fiber arrays for 800G/1.6T modules and CPO, CW DFB and EML laser chips, MPO/MMC high-density connector jumpers and data-center indoor cables

quarterly_data.quarter: Shijia Photons annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 2025 results: revenue RMB 212,912.48 ten-thousand, up 98.15% YoY; net profit attributable to shareholders RMB 37,222.85 ten-thousand, up 473.25%; net profit excluding non-recurring items RMB 37,089.75 ten-thousand, up 670.45%; operating cash flow RMB 7,455.63 ten-thousand, up 190.59%. The company attributes the revenue growth to AI-driven rapid growth of the datacom market, stronger product competitiveness and customer recognition, with orders for optical chips and devices, indoor optical cable and cable polymer materials all up year on year; profit growth also reflected cost reduction and higher yields, partly offset by impairment provisions and the USD/RMB exchange-rate move (export business is mainly settled in US dollars). Operating cash flow lagged net profit because of inventory built for orders and receivables not yet due.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue RMB 212,912.48 ten-thousand (+98.15% YoY); net profit RMB 37,222.85 ten-thousand (+473.25%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Shijia Photons annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 2025 by product: optical chips and devices revenue RMB 159,101.97 ten-thousand, up 162.39% YoY, gross margin 36.05% (up 2.66 percentage points); indoor optical cable RMB 25,573.94 ten-thousand, up 16.91%, gross margin 26.84%; cable polymer materials RMB 25,138.97 ten-thousand, up 8.65%, gross margin 20.42%. Optical-communication main business gross margin 33.06%, up 6.70 points. Overseas revenue RMB 112,186.90 ten-thousand, up 300.34% YoY, 52.69% of 2025 revenue (gross margin 32.59%); domestic revenue up 25.77% (gross margin 33.60%). The company says the overseas jump is because datacom demand comes mainly from overseas customers.

quarterly_data.quarter: Shijia Photons annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 2025 production and sales: optical chips and devices produced 21,645.82 ten-thousand units (+75.81%), 7,000.18 ten-thousand used in-house, sold 13,451.12 ten-thousand units (+25.57%), ending inventory 2,240.30 ten-thousand (+114.22%); indoor optical cable produced 1,963,225.06 fiber-km (+67.54%), sold 993,047.36 fiber-km (+4.14%); cable materials produced 17,644.20 tonnes (-4.04%), sold 16,658.16 tonnes (-3.95%). quarterly_data.quarter: Shijia Photons annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Datacom passive products in 2025 (company): CWDM/LAN WDM AWG components for 400G and 800G modules shipped in large volume, and the company says it holds a main position in device supply for 100G-800G modules; multi-fiber high-density connectors (MMC / SN-MT) for 800G/1.6T networks are in volume shipments; its MMC high-density connector passed US Conec certification and its SN-MT connector passed SENKO certification; an 8-channel 200GHz AWG chip and component for AI optical computing reached small-batch shipments. CPO micro-optics R&D project (budget RMB 3,500,000.00): FAU-MT for CPO and a high-precision lidless FAU-MT are in small-batch shipments; silicon-photonics micro-optics project: high-temperature FAU samples delivered, double/triple-row FAU passed initial validation and a customer is designing its chip around the company's solution.

quarterly_data.quarter: Shijia Photons annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Silicon-photonics light sources (company): the CW DFB chip and TOSA device project (budget RMB 130,800,000.00, RMB 49,136,222.03 invested to date) reached volume shipments and was completed; the high-power DFB and high-speed EML laser chip project (budget RMB 23,000,000.00) passed project acceptance. The 2025 report says CW DFB laser chips completed validation at some customers with small-batch deliveries and the company is actively advancing capacity planning and production-line deployment for them; its EML prototype development has been gradually completed and is in customer validation.
quarterly_data.figure: CW DFB chip and TOSA project budget RMB 130,800,000.00 (completed)

quarterly_data.quarter: Shijia Photons annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Telecom passive products in 2025 (company): its DWDM AWG products entered the supply chains of mainstream domestic and overseas equipment makers in volume production; 60-channel 100GHz, 40-channel 150GHz, 17-channel 300GHz and 64-channel 75GHz AWG chips and modules for 200G/400G/800G coherent backbone and metro networks are shipping in volume; a 24-channel VOA array chip and 40/48/60-channel VMUX modules (SOI silicon-photonics scheme) are in volume shipments.

quarterly_data.quarter: Shijia Photons annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Overseas capacity: its Thailand subsidiary had 2025 revenue of RMB 195,402,178.37 and net profit of RMB 19,356,793.44; to advance the Thailand industrial-park project the company is raising the Thai subsidiary's registered capital, via a newly set-up Singapore subsidiary, by up to US$50 million (5,000 ten-thousand US dollars). The company says it is accelerating the Thai subsidiary's capacity build-out to offset trade-policy risk, as part of its products face higher US tariffs whether exported directly or indirectly, including through the Southeast Asian plant.

quarterly_data.quarter: Shijia Photons annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 2026 business plan (company, stated as forward-looking and not a commitment or profit forecast): in passive products, push customer validation and volume introduction of AWG chips and components for 1.6T modules and industrialise large-channel polarisation-maintaining devices and high-temperature FAU for CPO; in active products, speed up CW DFB laser-chip customer validation and finalise and sample EML laser chips; steadily advance expansion projects in Hebi and Thailand for high-speed optical chips and devices, fiber connector jumpers and indoor cable; and look for acquisition targets that fit its strategy.
